evidence.claim: Toast describes itself as an all-in-one digital technology platform built for hospitality and reported record net location additions and ARR growth in 2025.
Toast filings describe online ordering, Order & Pay, marketing, loyalty, and restaurant online-ordering channels as tools that may help restaurants save on third-party commissions.

PAR's 2025 10-K describes Engagement Cloud, including Punchh/PAR Engagement and PAR Ordering, for loyalty, engagement, omnichannel digital ordering, and delivery; it also describes Operator Cloud including PAR POS, PAR Pay, and back-office products.
NCR Voyix's 2026 Q1 filing says it operates Retail and Restaurants segments and that restaurant solutions include POS hardware/software, payment processing, and merchant services.
SoundHound's 2025 Form 10-K discusses plans to expand customer partnerships and roll out AI drive-thru services and dynamic restaurant ordering capabilities.

Olo was a highly relevant restaurant ordering, payment, and guest-engagement software public comp, but Thoma Bravo completed its acquisition and Olo's common stock ceased trading and was delisted from NYSE in 2025.

memory_update.text: PAR is a priority underfollowed candidate for restaurant loyalty, ordering, POS, payments, and customer-data infrastructure; verify subscription metrics, customer wins, retention, and enterprise chain exposure.
NCR Voyix is a messy but direct restaurant commerce infrastructure candidate; verify restaurant segment economics after spin/sale simplification and avoid over-crediting retail exposure.

SoundHound AI belongs in the speculative shadow lane for restaurant voice ordering and drive-thru automation; require restaurant-specific revenue, deployment, and integration evidence before upgrading.

Olo was one of the cleanest public restaurant ordering and guest-engagement software comps but is no longer US-listed after the 2025 Thoma Bravo acquisition; use it as a private-market comp, not a candidate.

node: Delivery marketplace access, first-party ordering, loyalty, POS, and restaurant customer-data infrastructure
summary: Layer 1B expands the public-market universe around restaurant customer access and data ownership. The obvious reference name is Toast, which has the cleanest public restaurant-tech mapping. The discovery lane is PAR Technology and NCR Voyix, both smaller and messier software/POS names with direct exposure to restaurant ordering, loyalty, POS, payments, and operational data. SoundHound AI is included as a speculative shadow candidate for drive-thru and phone-ordering automation, but its AI attention level and diversified enterprise positioning require stricter evidence checks.
